newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Feb 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Feb 25.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Part of the staff at Poldi Steel will begin an indefinite strike this morning. They want their wages paid, at least for November. About 200 workers will participate in the strike.

- Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy urged the coalition yesterday to reach a decision soon on fast changes in energy prices. The coalition parties should clearly state their opinions on regulated energy prices and rents and on certain tax questions in a conference this Thursday.
PRAVO - This January, exports decreased by 2.5 percent in comparison to January of 1996. Imports, however increased by 8.2 percent. The trade deficit was 13.6 billion crowns.

- Surprisingly, Chemapol Group withdrew its participation in the tender for a strategic partner for Aero Vodochody. Shortly before the announcement to withdraw, the management of Chemapol stated that it will not even compete for a share in Unipetrol.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - A wide variety of companies owe the state treasury more than 35 billion crowns for taxes since 1993. The state can write off nearly nine billion of this. Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik explains that world experience shows that one quarter of unpaid taxes is, as a rule, irretrievable, and for this reason, the state grants general pardons from time to time.
- Prague Breweries, one of the three largest domestic beer producers, will increase its wholesale prices from March on average by four to five percent on some of its brands including Staropramen.

- CKD Praha and Skodaexport, which were members of the business mission accompanying Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus in his visit to Canada, have made a preliminary agreement for cooperative work with various Canadian businesses.

LIDOVE NOVINY - The former director of the secret service (BIS), Stanislav Devaty, won in a judicial dispute with the Social Democratic Party (CSSD). According to the ruling from the Municipal Court in Prague, CSSD must pay him one million crowns in compensation for false accusations, and the chairman of CSSD, Milos Zeman, must make a public apology to Devaty.

- Foreign Minister Josef Zieleniec rejected the idea of organising a refererendum for entry of the Czech Republic into NATO. He believes that it would create a confrontational atmosphere in the country.
